summary.text: In water, oxygen saturation compares the dissolved oxygen present with the most that water could hold at its temperature and pressure.
Fish, invertebrates, plants and aerobic bacteria all need oxygen, and in an estuary the best dissolved oxygen level is above six ppm.
When decaying matter or nutrient pollution drains the oxygen, fish are pushed out and fish kills can follow.

items.prompt: Can a still pond ever hold more oxygen than its normal full-saturation level?

options.label: No, full saturation is a hard limit
Yes, if water plants or algae are making oxygen
Only if the pond freezes over
Only if the water is salty

items.explain: Stagnant water can become supersaturated, above 100%, when photosynthetic oxygen producers are present or after a slow adjustment to changed air conditions.

items.prompt: A fast, splashing stream has no plants or animals adding or using oxygen. What is its likely oxygen saturation?

options.label: About 50%
Over 200%

items.explain: Well-aerated water without oxygen producers or consumers sits at 100% saturation.

items.prompt: A stagnant pond is choked with rotting leaves. What would you expect a dissolved oxygen reading to show?

options.label: Far less oxygen than the water could hold
More oxygen than the water could normally hold
Exactly the most oxygen the water could hold
The same reading as a fast mountain stream

items.explain: Stagnant water with decaying matter typically sits well below 100% oxygen saturation.

items.prompt: Nutrient pollution drives oxygen in a river very low. Which of these tends to suffer?

options.label: Bacteria that thrive without oxygen
No living things are affected
Fish
Only creatures living in salt water

items.explain: Low oxygen suppresses aerobic organisms such as fish and favours anaerobic ones, which can lead to fish kills.

items.prompt: A water test reports a lake at 80% oxygen saturation. What two amounts is that figure comparing?

options.label: Oxygen in the lake versus oxygen in the air above
Oxygen versus carbon dioxide in the lake
This year's oxygen versus last year's
Dissolved oxygen versus the most the water could hold

items.explain: Saturation is the dissolved oxygen concentration as a share of the maximum that will dissolve at that temperature and pressure.

items.prompt: A fish farmer wants to check how much oxygen is dissolved in a tank. Which tool fits the job?

options.label: A pulse oximeter on a finger
A pH test strip
An oxygen sensor or optode probe
A simple glass thermometer

items.explain: Dissolved oxygen in water is measured with a probe such as an oxygen sensor or optode, while pulse oximetry measures oxygen in blood.
